description: Reusable OT countermeasure examples mapped to the example threat keys in this repository knowledge base.

countermeasures.title: Authenticate write operations and constrain unsafe protocol commands
countermeasures.description: Add role separation, authenticated sessions, command allow-lists, and process-aware write restrictions for engineering and protocol write paths.

countermeasures.title: Enforce signed updates and anti-rollback protections
countermeasures.description: Require authenticated firmware packages, protected key storage, measured boot, and version monotonicity checks before activation.

countermeasures.title: Disable, lock, or monitor debug and service ports in production
countermeasures.description: Fuse off unused debug interfaces, require authenticated enablement for service ports, and detect local maintenance access attempts.

countermeasures.title: Eliminate default commissioning credentials and rotate pairing secrets
countermeasures.description: Force unique per-device onboarding credentials, credential rotation, failed-attempt lockout, and time-bounded service enablement for wireless maintenance features.

countermeasures.title: Protect telemetry with authentication and freshness checks
countermeasures.description: Use message authentication, counters, timestamps, or sequence checks so replayed or forged sensor and actuator traffic is rejected.

countermeasures.title: Rate-limit protocol handling and define safe degraded behavior
countermeasures.description: Harden protocol parsing, rate-limit expensive requests, isolate fragile services, and define deterministic fail-safe behavior when communications are disrupted.
